bull.b: Owning 26 MW of energized capacity at low blended power costs provides a durable operating foundation for bitcoin mining and potential AI/HPC hosting. This infrastructure can support higher utilization, improve cost competitiveness, and give management flexibility to expand across multiple compute applications.

bull.t: Mining fleet efficiency and hashrate expansion
bull.b: Replacing older machines with S19 XP units raises hashrate by nearly 39% per replacement at similar power draw, while planned deployments increase total capacity. This should improve productive use of existing infrastructure and support incremental revenue without requiring an equivalent expansion in power consumption.

bull.t: Improving mining output and sequential margin
bull.b: Higher bitcoin production and sequentially improved mining margin indicate better operating execution in the core mining business. Although profitability remains weak, stronger output and improved economics can provide a more scalable revenue base if the company sustains fleet uptime, efficiency, and disciplined energy management.

bear.t: Severe losses and negative cash generation
bear.b: The company is operating with sharply negative gross profit, very large net losses, and substantial cash burn, showing that current activities are not self-funding. Persistent negative cash generation can require repeated financing or asset sales, limiting investment capacity and weakening resilience over the next several quarters.

bear.t: High leverage and collateralized refinancing risk
bear.b: Rising leverage has reduced the equity buffer, while bitcoin-backed borrowing exposes the company to collateral and renewal pressure. The short-duration facility may lower stated interest costs, but dependence on frequent refinancing can constrain strategy and intensify liquidity risk if collateral values or lending conditions weaken.

The AI/HPC pivot has not yet demonstrated material commercial traction, so it cannot currently offset weakness in the existing business. Illustrative long-term revenue estimates depend on capital and customer contracts that are not secured, making execution, funding, and conversion of power capacity into revenue uncertain.
